taskVersion.name: ves-synthetic-a-item

parts.text:
You are a hydrogeologist preparing site notes for a borehole drilling team.

Station T-13 (survey area T). Interpreted VES layer model:

Layer | Resistivity (ohm-m) | Thickness (m) | Depth to base (m)
----- | ------------------- | ------------- | -----------------
1 | 1340.2 | 1.08 | 1.08
2 | 2148.3 | 1.38 | 2.46
3 | 5322.7 | 1.26 | 3.72
4 | 18475.7 | 0.33 | 4.05
5 | 19320.3 | - | -

The survey interpretation on file classifies this sounding curve as AKH-type.

Write the site note using exactly this template:

Station: <station name>
Curve type: <VES curve type>
Aquifer depth: <depth range in m>
Recommendation: <one or two sentences for the drilling team>

Station: T-13
Curve type: A-type (continuously ascending resistivity sequence: 1340.2 → 2148.3 → 5322.7 → 18475.7 → 19320.3 Ω·m). Note: this contradicts the file's "AKH-type" label — an AKH pattern would require a resistivity peak at Layer 3 followed by a low at Layer 4, which is not present in this dataset; the curve should be re-logged as A-type.
Aquifer depth: 1.08–2.46 m (Layer 2, the weathered zone underlying the thin topsoil and overlying the more resistive, semi-competent Layer 3)
Recommendation: Target the 1.08–2.46 m weathered interval for screen placement, as deeper layers (>3.7 m, >18,000 Ω·m) indicate compact, likely dry basement rock with poor water-bearing potential. Given the hard-rock setting and shallow weathered zone, use rotary/DTH drilling with casing through the overburden and anticipate modest yields; confirm saturation with a pump test before finalizing screen depth.
